incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - Latency SLO breach detected for streaming inference in us-west-2.
Details: p95=320ms (SLO 200ms), p99=1.6s (SLO 500ms). Streaming stalls / tail spikes observed across several clusters.
Signal: gpu-group gpu-45 showing burst of correctable ECCs + fan speed >95% + thermal throttle flags. Paging oncall.

jane (oncall-sre): acknowledged. I'm taking incident lead. tagging roles - @miguel for runtime, @ryan for infra coord, @katie for customer impact.

miguel (eng-runtime): collecting traces and KV cache stats now. early look shows repeated prefix cache misses causing longer token generations, and some requests hitting nodes with high GPU stall counts. pulling nvml.

miguel (eng-runtime): logs/snippet:
```
GPU 45: temperature 92C, fan 98%, perf_throttle_reason: 0x38 (thermal + power),
ECC correctable: recent delta 120 -> 187 (surge),
streams_inflight: 460 -> 520, avg_batch_size: 6.1 -> 9.4
```

ryan (eng-sre): thanks. prepping live mitigation. recommendation: cordon+drain the hot nodes + route traffic to warm spare pool. reduce batching on streaming endpoints during spill.
ryan (eng-sre): commands I'm about to run:
```bash
kubectl -n inference cordon gpu-node-172
kubectl -n inference drain gpu-node-172 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# adjust routing to spare pool
redwoodctl route set --route=streaming-usw2 --pool=warm-spare --reason="live mitigation - gpu thermal"
# temporarily cap batch size for streaming workers
redwoodctl config set --service=streaming --key=max_batch_size --value=4
```

jane (oncall-sre): execute when ready. I'll monitor p95/p99 and error rates. set incident channel to high-visibility. notify SRE pager.

katie (support): queue shows 8 customers with retries / degraded streaming quality. one enterprise (acme-inc) reported multiple chat timeouts ~2pm PST. I opened a priority ticket and informed account team. putting affected customer list in incident doc.

anna (product): flagging contract-impact risk for ACME. small window but they have SLAs. need exec notification if this goes past 1 hour.

miguel (eng-runtime): running lightweight probe against node set to confirm serialization stalls -> observed streaming stalls align with GPU throttle windows. also seeing KV spill metrics increase: `kv_cache_evictions` spiked during the event.

miguel (eng-runtime): more raw diagnostics:
```
# nvml smi sample
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 530.30.02    Driver Version: 530.30.02    CUDA Version: 12.1   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Temp  Fan  Perf  ECC_Corr  Pwr Draw  Throttle |
| 45   A100-SXM4    92C   98%  P0    187        320W      THERMAL
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

ryan (eng-sre): starting drains now for nodes: gpu-node-172, gpu-node-174. routing change queued. will monitor rollback-safe window (15m).

incident-bot: update: routing change applied to warm-spare. drains submitted for 2 nodes.

jane (oncall-sre): initial metrics after routing - p95 dropped to 210ms, p99 at 580ms. still above target but improving. error rates for streaming retries down 40%. continuing.

lee (customer-success): pinging account managers for top 5 affected customers, prepping postmortem template and timeline for stakeholders.

ryan (eng-sre): one caution - warm-spare pool running mixed GPU generations; we enabled model-compatible fallbacks to reduce model mismatch issues. watch for quality regressions.

katie (support): ACME wants a status update. giving interim: "We detected underlying hardware thermal events impacting inference latency, we've routed your traffic away from affected nodes and mitigations are in place, we'll follow up with timeline and next steps."

miguel (eng-runtime): quick note - KV cache warmup might cause temporary p95 variance as traffic warms second pool. expecting stabilization in 10-15m.

george (oncall-next): I'm up next. taking over monitoring and vendor coord for hardware RMA. please handoff open actions: 1) ensure drains complete cleanly, 2) file RMA for GPU-45, 3) run post-drain regression test on a canary stream.

jane (oncall-sre): handoff done. open actions: RMA ticket to vendor (priority high), follow-up root-cause (ECC surge origin), run bake window 60m, update affected customers list. tagging @george.

incident-bot: status update: mitigated -> routing + drains reduced p95 to 180ms, p99 to 420ms. errors down to baseline +15%. marking incident as mitigated; remains P1 until hardware replacement confirmed.

anna (product): confirm we should notify execs? I can draft a short summary and send after final p99 <500ms for 30m.

katie (support): thanks. I'll close immediate tickets only after ACME confirms stability. will attach mitigation timeline.

miguel (eng-runtime): saved snapshots and perf counters to bucket gs://redwood-incident-dumps/1888887777/ for postmortem.

jane (oncall-sre): good work. final note - we'll keep the drain in place until RMA and run stress repro on isolated hardware to check for flaky ECC.

incident-bot: incident channel archived note queued. reactions: :thumbsup: :thermometer_face: :gear:
